_DRAFT: DRAFT — 20 November 2026. Do NOT rename this file to capacitor.config.json and do NOT run `npx cap add ios` / `npx cap add android` yet. Capacitor is not installed, there is no native project, no signing identity, and no deployed production URL to point at. This file only records the decisions made so far so the native build starts from a reviewed draft instead of from scratch. See the _notes array below for everything that must happen first.
_notes: appId is PROPOSED, not registered: com.rabiscomagico.app. Confirm nobody else holds it, confirm the legal entity / developer account that will own it, and lock it in before the first submission — the bundle id / application id cannot be changed after the first store submission.
appName matches the PWA manifest (public/manifest.json): Rabisco Magico.

webDir is public/ because there is no build step: public/ is the web root Express serves (server.js serves public/ as static files). If a build step is ever added, webDir must point at the build output instead.

LIVE-SERVER MODE IS REQUIRED — READ THIS FIRST: public/app.js calls the API with relative URLs (/api/transform, /api/gallery, /api/parent/*, /api/checkout/*). Inside a Capacitor shell the bundled pages load from capacitor://localhost (iOS) / https://localhost (Android), so a relative /api/... would hit the phone itself, not the server. This draft therefore sets server.url to the deployed web app. Until the API base is configurable in app.js, the native app is a wrapper around the live site, not an offline bundle. Do not ship a bundled-only build.

server.url is a PLACEHOLDER (https://__DEPLOYED_BASE_URL__). Replace it with the real production BASE_URL (the same value as the BASE_URL env var in .env.example) when the native project is created. cleartext is false: never allow plain http in production.

Service worker: public/app.js registers sw.js unconditionally. A service worker does not work reliably inside a Capacitor WebView and can fight the native shell's caching. Before the first native build, guard the registration so it only runs on the real web (e.g. skip when window.Capacitor is defined), and re-test the offline drawing board on a real device.

No native plugins are used yet. Download / share currently use web APIs (canvas download, navigator.share). Verify both on a real iOS and a real Android device in the native shell; if either fails, add @capacitor/share and @capacitor/filesystem at that point — do not add plugins speculatively.

What still needs a real native project before anything can build: (1) install Capacitor — npm i @capacitor/core @capacitor/cli — then rename this file to capacitor.config.json and run npx cap add ios and npx cap add android; (2) a Mac with Xcode for iOS and Android Studio for Android — npx cap add ios only works on macOS; (3) an Apple Developer account (paid) and a Google Play developer account, with the appId above registered in App Store Connect and Play Console; (4) code signing — an iOS distribution certificate + provisioning profile, and an Android upload key + Play App Signing; (5) a finished 1024x1024 PNG app icon (public/icon.svg is a placeholder — see docs/release-checklist.md) and splash assets, generated with @capacitor/assets; (6) the production server deployed and reachable at server.url, with FAL_KEY funded, Stripe live-mode decision made, and the output-safety check wired (see docs/kids-compliance-checklist.md) — the native shell does not fix any of those; (7) magic-link / Stripe return URLs re-checked as universal links / app links for the native shell, since the magic-link email flow is still a stub (lib/accounts.js).

Plugins in this draft are display-only defaults (splash screen, status bar) and must be reviewed when the native project exists. No analytics, advertising, or tracking plugin is included — deliberately. Adding one later needs a kids-compliance review first (see docs/store-kids-compliance.md): Apple Kids forbids third-party ads/analytics outright, Google Play Families allows only certified ad SDKs and no personalised ads.

iOS: contentInset always, so the drawing board is not hidden behind the notch / home indicator. Android: allowMixedContent false. Both are defaults worth keeping; verify on a real device with the smallest supported screen.

Do NOT commit ios/ or android/ until the native projects exist and have been reviewed — they contain generated native code and signing config. When they are added, .gitignore must cover local signing files (see the Capacitor docs at that point).
